sentences.zh: 任顓，字誠之，青州壽光人。

translations.literal: Ren Zhuan, styled Chengzhi, was a man of Shouguang in Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhuan, whose courtesy name was Chengzhi, came from Shouguang in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，得同學究出身。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and received appointment at the tong xue jiu level.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and entered service with the inferior tong xue jiu qualification.

sentences.zh: 至衛尉丞。

translations.literal: He rose to Vice Director of the Imperial Insignia Office.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to the post of Vice Director of the Imperial Insignia Office.

sentences.zh: 上其文，乃賜第，擢鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: When he submitted his writings, he was granted a ranked place in the palace examination and was promoted to Assistant Salt and Iron Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After he submitted his writings to the throne, he was granted a ranked place in the palace examination and was promoted to assistant commissioner of the Salt and Iron Commission.

sentences.zh: 陝西鑄康定大銅錢，顓曰：「壞五為一，以一當十，恐犯者眾。

translations.literal: When Shaanxi cast the large Kangding copper coins, Zhuan said, "Breaking five coins to make one, with one counted as ten, will likely make offenders numerous."
translations.idiomatic: When Shaanxi cast the large Kangding copper coins, Zhuan remarked, "Melting five coins into one and valuing it at ten will surely multiply the number of lawbreakers."

sentences.zh: 」卒如其言。

translations.literal: In the end it happened just as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end events unfolded exactly as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 夏人納款，遣使要請十一事，甚者欲去臣稱男。

translations.literal: When the Xia submitted allegiance, they sent envoys demanding eleven concessions, the most extreme being to remove their designation as subject and use "male" instead.
translations.idiomatic: When the Western Xia tendered submission, they sent envoys demanding eleven concessions, the most extreme of which was to drop their status as subjects and be addressed as "male" instead.

sentences.zh: 顓押伴，一切曉以義，辭折而去。

translations.literal: Zhuan served as escort commissioner; he explained righteousness in every matter, and they withdrew after being refuted in argument.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuan served as escort commissioner and explained the principles of righteousness in every matter until the envoys withdrew, their arguments defeated.

sentences.zh: 又再遣使來欲自買賣，且通青鹽，增歲賜，詔許置榷場，其議多顓所發。

translations.literal: They sent envoys again wishing to trade on their own, to obtain green salt, and to increase the annual gifts; an imperial decree permitted establishing monopoly markets, and many of these proposals had originated with Zhuan.
translations.idiomatic: They sent envoys again seeking permission to trade on their own, to obtain green salt, and to increase the annual gifts; the court authorized monopoly markets, and many of these proposals had originated with Zhuan.

sentences.zh: 出為京西轉運使，奏計京師。

translations.literal: He went out as Transport Commissioner of the Jingxi circuit and submitted annual accounts in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed transport commissioner of the Jingxi circuit and traveled to the capital to present the annual accounts.

sentences.zh: 元昊為下所殺，遣楊守素來告哀。

translations.literal: Yuanhao was killed by his subordinates, and they sent Yang Shousu to announce mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao was killed by his subordinates, and the Xia sent Yang Shousu to announce his death and seek mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 守素，乃始為元昊謀不稱臣、納賜節者也。

translations.literal: Shousu was the one who had first advised Yuanhao not to call himself subject and to reject the bestowal of investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Shousu was the very man who had first counseled Yuanhao to refuse the title of subject and to reject the imperial patent of investiture.

sentences.zh: 仁宗記嘗屈其使者，復使押伴，顓問守素其主所以死，不能對，訖去，不敢肆。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong remembered that their envoys had once been humiliated; Zhuan was again made escort commissioner. He asked Shousu how his lord had died, and Shousu could not answer; when he left he did not dare act insolently.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong recalled how their envoys had once been humiliated, and Zhuan was again assigned as escort commissioner. He asked Shousu how his lord had died; Shousu could not answer, and by the time he departed he no longer dared behave arrogantly.

sentences.zh: 改知鳳翔府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 帝語輔臣，顓宜備朝廷委任，留判三司恁由司。

translations.literal: The emperor told his chief ministers that Zhuan should be readied for court appointment and was retained as acting director of the Minyou Bureau under the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his chief ministers that Zhuan ought to be prepared for important court appointments and kept him in the capital as acting director of the Minyou Bureau under the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 為諒祚冊禮使，采摭西夏風物、山川、道里、出入攻取之要，為《治戎精要》三篇上之。

translations.literal: As investiture envoy for Liangzuo, he collected Western Xia products, mountains and rivers, routes, and key points for advance and withdrawal in attack and defense, and submitted three chapters entitled 《Essentials for Governing the Frontier》.
translations.idiomatic: As investiture envoy for Liangzuo, he gathered material on Western Xia customs, terrain, routes, and strategic points for advance and withdrawal, and submitted three chapters entitled 《Essentials for Governing the Frontier》.

sentences.zh: 進直史館，遷河東轉運使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to compiler in the Historiography Institute and transferred to transport commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to compiler in the Historiography Institute and appointed transport commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗以禁帑金帛賜河北，亦欲與河東，顓辭曰：「受委制財用，而先有求，不敢。

translations.literal: The emperor had once bestowed gold and silk from the privy treasury on Hebei and also wished to give some to Hedong. Zhuan declined, saying, "Having been entrusted to control finances, I dare not seek favors in advance."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had once bestowed gold and silk from the privy treasury on Hebei and wished to do the same for Hedong. Zhuan declined, saying, "Having been entrusted to manage public funds, I dare not seek favors in advance."

sentences.zh: 」顓為使者，每行部，必擇僚佐之賢者一人與俱，凡事必與議，未嘗以胥吏自隨，人安其政。

translations.literal: As a circuit commissioner, whenever he made an inspection tour he always chose one capable subordinate to accompany him; on every matter he consulted with him and never took clerks along, and the people were at ease under his administration.
translations.idiomatic: As a circuit commissioner, whenever he toured his jurisdiction he selected one capable aide to accompany him, consulted him on every matter, and never took clerks along with him, so that the people lived peacefully under his rule.

sentences.zh: 入為鹽鐵副使，擢天章閣待制。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Vice Commissioner of Salt and Iron and was promoted to Hanlin academician of the Tianzhang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as vice commissioner of the Salt and Iron Commission and was promoted to Hanlin academician of the Tianzhang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 儂賊犯嶺外，以知潭州。

translations.literal: When the Nong rebels invaded beyond the Ling ranges, he was appointed prefect of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nong rebels raided the region south of the Ling ranges, he was appointed prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣撫司以宣毅卒有功，檄補軍校，顓察其色動，曰：「必有異志。

translations.literal: The Pacification Commission ordered that a Xuanyi soldier who had rendered service be appointed a military officer. Zhuan observed that his expression shifted and said, "He must harbor ulterior intent."
translations.idiomatic: The Pacification Commission ordered that a Xuanyi soldier who had distinguished himself be appointed a military officer. Zhuan noticed a change in his expression and said, "This man must harbor ulterior designs."

sentences.zh: 」執按之，具服為賊內應。

translations.literal: He had the man seized and interrogated, and he fully confessed to acting as the rebels' agent within.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuan had him arrested and interrogated, and the man fully confessed to serving as the rebels' agent within the city.

sentences.zh: 搜其家，得所記潭事甚悉，梟首以徇。

translations.literal: A search of his home yielded very detailed records of affairs in Tan, and his head was displayed as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: A search of his home turned up detailed records of affairs in Tanzhou, and his head was displayed as a warning to others.

sentences.zh: 詔書褒激，賜白金五百兩，進龍圖閣直學士、知渭州。

translations.literal: An imperial edict praised and rewarded him with five hundred taels of white silver, and he was promoted to academician of the Longtu Pavilion and appointed prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict praised his achievement and rewarded him with five hundred taels of white silver; he was promoted to academician of the Longtu Pavilion and appointed prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 坐在潭日，賤市死商珠，降為待制。

translations.literal: Because while in Tan he had bought at low price pearls from a dead merchant, he was demoted to Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Because while serving in Tanzhou he had bought at a low price pearls from a deceased merchant, he was demoted to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 時四路以邊警聞，渭獨無所上，朝廷疑斥候不密，顓力言無他虞，帝使覘之，信。

translations.literal: At the time all four frontier circuits reported border alarms, but Weizhou alone submitted nothing; the court suspected lax scouting. Zhuan strongly declared there was no other concern; the emperor sent someone to investigate and found it true.
translations.idiomatic: At the time all four frontier circuits reported border alarms, yet Weizhou alone sent no reports, and the court suspected lax scouting. Zhuan insisted there was no cause for alarm; the emperor sent someone to investigate and found him correct.

sentences.zh: 乃還學士，徙徐州，以太子賓客致仕。

translations.literal: He was then restored to academician, transferred to Xuzhou, and retired as Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was then restored to his academician rank, transferred to Xuzhou, and retired with the title Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 積官戶部侍郎，卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: Having accumulated office to Vice Minister of Revenue, he died at the age of seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Having risen to vice minister of revenue, he died at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 李參，字清臣，鄆州須城人。

translations.literal: Li Can, styled Qingchen, was a man of Xucheng in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Can, whose courtesy name was Qingchen, came from Xucheng in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 以蔭知鹽山縣。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he became magistrate of Yanshan County.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he was appointed magistrate of Yanshan County.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，諭富室出粟，平其直予民，不能糴者，給以糟籺，所活數萬。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he persuaded wealthy households to release grain, stabilized the price for the people, and for those unable to buy grain he gave them distillers' dregs and bran cakes, saving tens of thousands of lives.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year he persuaded wealthy households to release grain and stabilized the price for the people; those who could not afford to buy grain he supplied with distillers' dregs and bran cakes, saving tens of thousands of lives.

sentences.zh: 通判定州，都部署夏守恩貪濫不法，轉運使使參按之，得其事，守恩謫死。

translations.literal: As vice-prefect of Dingzhou he investigated Regional Commander-in-Chief Xia Shou'en, who was greedy and lawless at the instigation of the transport commissioner; the facts were established and Shou'en was demoted and died.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as vice-prefect of Dingzhou, he investigated Regional Commander-in-Chief Xia Shou'en, who was corrupt and lawless, at the transport commissioner's order; the case was proved, and Shou'en was demoted and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 知荊門軍，荊門歲以夏伐竹，並稅簿輸荊南造舟，積日久多蠹惡不可用，牙校破產不償責。

translations.literal: As military commissioner of Jingmen, he found that Jingmen each summer cut bamboo and, together with tax registers, shipped it to Jingnan for boat-building; over long accumulation much rotted and became unusable, and military officers went bankrupt unable to meet their obligations.
translations.idiomatic: As military commissioner of Jingmen, he found that each summer Jingmen cut bamboo and, along with tax registers, shipped it to Jingnan for boat-building; over the years much of it rotted and became unusable, and military officers were ruined trying to meet their obligations.

sentences.zh: 參請冬伐竹，度其費以給，餘募商人與為市，遂除其害。

translations.literal: Can requested that bamboo be cut in winter, estimated the costs for provision, and had merchants contracted for the remainder, thereby removing the abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Can proposed cutting bamboo in winter, estimating costs for local provision and contracting merchants for the surplus, thereby eliminating the abuse.

sentences.zh: 歷知興元府，淮南、京西、陝西轉運使。

translations.literal: He successively served as prefect of Xingyuan and as transport commissioner of Huainan, Jingxi, and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as prefect of Xingyuan and as transport commissioner of Huainan, Jingxi, and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 部多戍兵，苦食少。

translations.literal: His jurisdiction had many garrison troops who suffered from insufficient food.
translations.idiomatic: His jurisdiction had many garrison troops who suffered from chronic food shortages.

sentences.zh: 參審訂其闕，令民自隱度麥粟之贏，先貸以錢，俟穀熟還之官，號「青苗錢」，經數年，廩有羨糧。

translations.literal: Can examined and corrected the shortfall, ordering the people themselves to estimate their surplus wheat and grain, lending them money in advance to be repaid to the government when the grain ripened; this was called "green seedlings money." After several years the granaries held surplus grain.
translations.idiomatic: Can examined the shortfall and ordered the people to estimate their surplus wheat and grain themselves, lending them money in advance to be repaid when the harvest came in; this was called "green seedlings money." After several years the granaries held surplus grain.

sentences.zh: 熙寧青苗法，蓋萌於此矣。

translations.literal: The Green Seedlings Law of the Xining era had its origin in this.
translations.idiomatic: The Green Seedlings Law of the Xining era had its origin in this practice.

sentences.zh: 朝廷患邊費益廣，參建議輦錢邊郡，以平估糴，權罷入中法。

translations.literal: The court was troubled that frontier expenses grew ever larger; Can proposed transporting money to frontier prefectures to buy grain at fair valuation and temporarily suspending the tribute-entry method.
translations.idiomatic: As frontier expenses continued to mount, Can proposed shipping money to frontier prefectures to purchase grain at fair prices and temporarily suspending the tribute-entry method.

sentences.zh: 比其去，省榷貨錢千萬計。

translations.literal: By the time he left, monopoly-goods revenue had been reduced by tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he left office, monopoly-goods expenditures had been reduced by tens of millions of strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 召為鹽鐵副使，以右諫議大夫為河北都轉運使。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Vice Commissioner of Salt and Iron and, with the rank of Right Remonstrance Grand Master, became Chief Transport Commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice commissioner of the Salt and Iron Commission and, with the rank of Right Remonstrance Grand Master, appointed chief transport commissioner of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 與安撫使郭申錫相視決河，議不協；

translations.literal: Together with Pacification Commissioner Guo Shenxi he inspected the Yellow River breach, but their views did not agree;
translations.idiomatic: Together with Pacification Commissioner Guo Shenxi he inspected the Yellow River breach, but they could not agree on a course of action;

sentences.zh: 又與真定呂溱相惡，二人皆得罪，參移使河東，知荊南。

translations.literal: he also bore ill will toward Lü Zhen of Zhending; both men were punished, and Can was transferred to Hedong and appointed military commissioner of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: he also clashed with Lü Zhen of Zhending; both men were punished, and Can was transferred to serve in Hedong and as military commissioner of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐七年，召為三司使，參知政事孫抃曰：「參為主計，外臺將承風刻剝天下，天下之民困矣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiayou he was summoned as Commissioner of the Three Departments. Vice Grand Councillor Sun Bian said, "If Can becomes chief of finance, the outer offices will take their cue and exploit the empire; the people of the realm will be distressed."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiayou (1062) he was summoned as commissioner of the Three Departments. Vice Grand Councillor Sun Bian said, "If Can takes charge of finance, the outer offices will follow his lead and exploit the empire, and the people will be driven to ruin."

sentences.zh: 」乃改群牧使。

translations.literal: He was therefore changed to Commissioner of the Pasturage Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore reassigned as commissioner of the Pasturage Commission instead.

sentences.zh: 詔王安石、王陶置局經度國計，參言：「官各有職，臣若不任事，當從廢黜。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wang Anshi and Wang Tao to establish a bureau to plan state finance. Can said, "Each office has its duties; if I am not fit for my post, I should be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Wang Anshi and Wang Tao to establish a bureau to plan state finances. Can said, "Each office has its proper duties; if I am unfit for mine, I should be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 不然，乞罷此局。

translations.literal: Otherwise, I beg that this bureau be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, I beg that this bureau be abolished."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted his request.

sentences.zh: 治平初，加集賢院學士、知瀛州，賜黃金百兩，帥臣有賜自參始。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhiping era he was given the additional title of Academician of the Jixian Academy and appointed prefect of Yingzhou, and was granted one hundred taels of gold; the bestowal of gifts on frontier commanders began with Can.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhiping era (1064) he was given the additional title of academician of the Jixian Academy and appointed prefect of Yingzhou, and was granted one hundred taels of gold; the practice of bestowing gifts on frontier commanders began with Can.

sentences.zh: 再遷樞密直學士、知秦州。

translations.literal: He was again transferred as academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and appointed prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and appointed prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 蕃酋藥家族作亂，討平之，得良田五百頃，以募弓箭手。

translations.literal: The tribal chieftain of the Yao family rebelled; he suppressed the rebellion and obtained five hundred qing of fertile land, which he used to recruit archer militia.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribal chieftain of the Yao clan rebelled, he suppressed the uprising and obtained five hundred qing of fertile land, which he used to recruit archer militia.

sentences.zh: 居鎮閱歲，未嘗以邊事聞。

translations.literal: He held the post for about a year and never once reported a frontier incident.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post for about a year without once reporting a frontier incident to the court.

sentences.zh: 英宗遣使問故，對曰：「將在邊，期於無事而已，不敢妄以寇貽主憂。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong sent an envoy to ask the reason. He replied, "A general on the frontier should aim only for peace and dare not lightly burden his lord with reports of raids."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong sent an envoy to ask why. He replied, "A frontier commander should aim only to keep the border quiet and dare not lightly trouble his sovereign with alarms of enemy raids."

sentences.zh: 」以疾解邊任，判西京御史臺，起知曹、濮二州。

translations.literal: Because of illness he relinquished his frontier post, served as administrator of the Western Capital Censorate, and was later appointed prefect of Cao and Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Illness obliged him to leave his frontier post; he served as administrator of the Western Capital Censorate and was later appointed prefect of Cao and Pu.

sentences.zh: 神宗久知其才，書姓名於殿柱。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong had long known his talent and wrote his name on a palace pillar.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong had long recognized his ability and wrote his name on a palace pillar.

sentences.zh: 以知永興軍，不行，卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: He was appointed military commissioner of Yongxing but did not take up the post and died at the age of seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military commissioner of Yongxing but did not take up the post and died at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 參無學術，然剛果嚴深，喜發擿奸伏，不假貸，事至即決，雖簿書纖悉不遺，時稱能吏。

translations.literal: Can had no scholarly learning, yet he was resolute, strict, and penetrating, delighting in exposing hidden wrongdoing and showing no leniency; when a matter arose he decided it at once, and though he neglected no detail in documents, he was called a capable official.
translations.idiomatic: Can had little scholarly learning, yet he was resolute, strict, and penetrating, delighting in exposing hidden wrongdoing without mercy; when a case arose he decided it at once, and though he neglected no detail in official paperwork, contemporaries hailed him as a capable administrator.

sentences.zh: 郭申錫

translations.literal: Guo Shenxi
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shenxi

sentences.zh: 郭申錫，字延之，魏人。

translations.literal: Guo Shenxi, styled Yanzhi, was a man of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shenxi, whose courtesy name was Yanzhi, was a native of Wei.

sentences.zh: 自言唐代公元振之後。

translations.literal: He said of himself that he was a descendant of Yuan Zhen of the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed descent from Yuan Zhen of the Tang dynasty.

sentences.zh: 第進士，為晉陵尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and became sheriff of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed sheriff of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 民訴弟為人所殺，申錫察其色懼而哭不哀，曰：「吾得賊矣，非汝乎？

translations.literal: A man complained that his younger brother had been killed by someone. Shenxi observed that his expression showed fear and his weeping was not mournful, and said, "I have found the culprit—is it not you?"
translations.idiomatic: A man reported that his younger brother had been murdered. Shenxi noticed that the man's expression showed fear and his weeping lacked genuine grief, and said, "I have found the killer—is it not you?"

sentences.zh: 」執而訊之，果然。

translations.literal: He seized and interrogated him, and it proved true.
translations.idiomatic: He had the man arrested and interrogated him, and the confession proved true.

sentences.zh: 久之，知博州。

translations.literal: After some time he became prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 州兵出戍，有欲脅眾為亂者，申錫戮一人，黥二人，乃定。

translations.literal: When the prefectural troops went out on garrison duty, some wished to coerce the masses into rebellion; Shenxi executed one man and tattooed two, and order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When the prefectural troops went out on garrison duty, some plotted to coerce the men into mutiny; Shenxi executed one and branded two, and order was restored.

sentences.zh: 奏至，仁宗曰：「小官臨事如此，豈易得？

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, Emperor Renzong said, "For a minor official to handle affairs like this—is he not hard to come by?"
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, Emperor Renzong said, "For a minor official to handle affairs with such decisiveness—is such a man easy to find?"

sentences.zh: 」即為御史臺推直官。

translations.literal: He was immediately made investigating censor of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately appointed investigating censor of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 數上疏論事，大臣不便。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials discussing affairs, to the discomfort of the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly submitted memorials on public affairs, to the discomfort of the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 鞫獄慶州。

translations.literal: He conducted a judicial investigation in Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He conducted a judicial investigation in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 京東盜執濮州通判井淵，遷知州事，未閱月，悉擒凶黨，斬以徇。

translations.literal: Bandits in Jingdong seized Puzhou Vice-Prefect Jing Yuan; Shenxi was transferred to administer the prefecture, and within less than a month he captured the entire gang of ringleaders and executed them as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits in Jingdong seized Puzhou Vice-Prefect Jing Yuan; Shenxi was transferred to administer the prefecture, and within less than a month he captured the entire gang and executed them as a warning.

sentences.zh: 召為侍御史，遂知雜事。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Attending Censor and then took charge of miscellaneous business.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as attending censor and then took charge of miscellaneous censorial business.

sentences.zh: 張貴妃追冊、起園陵，張堯佐為使相，陳執中嬖妾殺婢，余靖引胡恢有醜行，高若訥引范祥啟邊釁，申錫皆奏劾之，屢詆權幸無所避，帝謂之曰：「近世士大夫，方未達時，好指陳時事，及被進用則不然，是資言以進耳，卿勿為也。」

translations.literal: When Consort Zhang was posthumously ennobled and a garden mausoleum was raised, when Zhang Yaozuo became commissioner-envoy and chancellor, when Chen Zhizhong's favorite concubine killed a maid, when Yu Jing recommended Hu Hui for disgraceful conduct, and when Gao Ruonu cited Fan Xiang for provoking border trouble, Shenxi memorialized impeachment in every case, repeatedly denouncing the powerful without avoidance. The emperor said to him, "In recent times, when scholar-officials have not yet attained office they like to point out current affairs, but once promoted they do not do so—this is using words to advance. Do not do this."
translations.idiomatic: When Consort Zhang was posthumously ennobled and a garden mausoleum was raised, when Zhang Yaozuo became commissioner-envoy and chancellor, when Chen Zhizhong's favorite concubine killed a maid, when Yu Jing recommended Hu Hui despite his disgraceful conduct, and when Gao Ruonu cited Fan Xiang for provoking border trouble, Shenxi memorialized impeachment in every case, repeatedly denouncing the powerful without fear. The emperor told him, "In recent times scholar-officials love to criticize current affairs before they attain office, but once promoted they cease—this is using words merely to advance. You must not do this."

sentences.zh: 諜稱契丹遣泛使，命體量安撫河北，還為鹽鐵副使。

translations.literal: Intelligence reported that the Khitan were sending a general envoy; he was ordered to assess and pacify Hebei, and on his return became Vice Commissioner of Salt and Iron.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligence reported that the Khitan were sending a general envoy; he was ordered to assess and pacify Hebei, and on his return was appointed vice commissioner of the Salt and Iron Commission.

sentences.zh: 相視決河，坐訟李參失實，黜知濠州。

translations.literal: While inspecting the Yellow River breach together, he was punished for prosecuting Li Can on false grounds and was demoted to prefect of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting the Yellow River breach together, he was punished for prosecuting Li Can on false grounds and was demoted to prefect of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 帝明榜朝堂，稱其欺誣，以儆在位。

translations.literal: The emperor posted a clear notice in the court hall calling his conduct deceitful, to warn those in office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor posted a clear notice in the court hall denouncing his deceit, to warn those in office.

sentences.zh: 旋加直史館、知江寧府，再副鹽鐵，進天章閣待制、知鄧州河中。

translations.literal: He was soon given concurrent appointment in the Historiography Institute, appointed prefect of Jiangning, again made vice commissioner of Salt and Iron, and promoted to Hanlin academician of the Tianzhang Pavilion and prefect of Dengzhou and Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given concurrent appointment in the Historiography Institute and appointed prefect of Jiangning, again served as vice commissioner of the Salt and Iron Commission, and was promoted to Hanlin academician of the Tianzhang Pavilion and prefect of Dengzhou and Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 种諤取綏州，申錫曰：「邊患將自此始。

translations.literal: When Zhong E seized Suizhou, Shenxi said, "Frontier troubles will begin from this."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong E seized Suizhou, Shenxi said, "Frontier troubles will begin from this act."

sentences.zh: 」及諒祚死，請捐前故，聽其子襲爵，且言曰：「二虜賴歲幣甚厚，渝平豈其所利，必有以致之。

translations.literal: When Liangzuo died, he requested setting aside past grievances and allowing his son to inherit the title, and further said, "The two barbarian states rely heavily on the annual gifts; breaking the peace cannot benefit them—there must be something that brought this about."
translations.idiomatic: When Liangzuo died, he asked that past grievances be set aside and that his son be allowed to inherit the title, adding, "The two barbarian states depend heavily on the annual gifts; breaking the peace cannot benefit them—something must have provoked this."

sentences.zh: 但得重將守邊，不要功生事，則善矣。

translations.literal: If only heavy generals guard the frontier and do not seek merit by stirring up trouble, that will be best."
translations.idiomatic: If only capable generals guard the frontier without seeking merit by stirring up trouble, that will suffice."

sentences.zh: 」著《邊鄙守禦策》。

translations.literal: He wrote 《Strategies for Defending the Frontier Borders》.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote 《Strategies for Defending the Frontier Borders》.

sentences.zh: 以給事中致仕，卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: He retired as Supervising Censor and died at the age of seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He retired with the title Supervising Censor and died at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 傅求，字命之，考城人。

translations.literal: Fu Qiu, styled Mingzhi, was a man of Kaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Qiu, whose courtesy name was Mingzhi, came from Kaocheng.

sentences.zh: 進士甲科，通判泗州。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the first class and became vice-prefect of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the first class and was appointed vice-prefect of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 淮水溢，毀城。

translations.literal: The Huai River overflowed and destroyed the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai River overflowed and destroyed the city walls.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣中使護築，絕淮取土，道遠，度用兵六十萬。

translations.literal: The court sent a palace envoy to supervise construction; earth was to be taken from across the Huai, the route was long, and labor was estimated at six hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent a palace envoy to supervise reconstruction; earth was to be taken from across the Huai, the haul was long, and labor was estimated at six hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 求相汴堤旁有高埠，夷之得土，載以回舟，省工費殆半。

translations.literal: Qiu observed that beside the Bian embankment there was a high mound; leveling it yielded earth, which was shipped on returning boats, saving nearly half the labor costs.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu observed a high mound beside the Bian embankment; leveling it provided earth, which returning boats carried back, saving nearly half the labor costs.

sentences.zh: 徙大名府，府守呂夷簡委以事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Daming Prefecture, where the prefect Lü Yijian entrusted him with affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Daming Prefecture, where Prefect Lü Yijian entrusted him with important affairs.

sentences.zh: 夷簡入相，薦其才，擢知宿州，提點江西、益州刑獄，為梓州路轉運使。

translations.literal: When Yijian entered the chancellorship he recommended Qiu's talent; Qiu was promoted to prefect of Suzhou, made judicial intendant of Jiangxi and Yizhou, and appointed transport commissioner of the Zizhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Yijian became chief councillor he recommended Qiu's ability; Qiu was promoted to prefect of Suzhou, appointed judicial intendant of Jiangxi and Yizhou, and made transport commissioner of the Zizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 夷獠寇合江，鈐轄司會兵掩擊，求馳往按所以狀，乃縣吏冒取播州田，獠故恐而叛。

translations.literal: Yi and Liao raided Hejiang; the commandery office gathered troops for a surprise attack. Qiu hurried there to investigate the cause and found that county clerks had seized land in Bozhou by fraud, and the tribes had rebelled out of fear.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and Liao tribes raided Hejiang; the commandery office gathered troops for a surprise attack. Qiu hurried there to investigate and found that county clerks had seized Bozhou land by fraud, provoking the tribes to rebel out of fear.

sentences.zh: 即黥吏置嶺南，夷人聞之，散去。

translations.literal: He immediately tattooed the clerks and sent them to Lingnan; when the tribes heard of it they dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately branded the clerks and sent them to Lingnan; when the tribes heard of this they dispersed.

sentences.zh: 益州文彥博上其狀，進秩，徙陝西。

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo of Yizhou reported his conduct; Qiu was promoted in rank and transferred to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo of Yizhou reported his conduct to the court; Qiu was promoted in rank and transferred to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 關中行當十鐵錢，盜鑄不可計，求請變法。

translations.literal: In the Guanzhong region iron coins valued at ten were in circulation and illicit casting was beyond counting; Qiu requested a change in the law.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guanzhong region iron coins valued at ten were in circulation and illicit casting was beyond counting; Qiu requested a change in the currency law.

sentences.zh: 時州縣已散二百八十萬緡，亟下令更為當三。

translations.literal: By then the prefectures and counties had already distributed 2.8 million strings; he urgently ordered that they be changed to a value of three.
translations.idiomatic: By then the prefectures and counties had already distributed 2.8 million strings of cash; he urgently ordered that they be revalued at three.

sentences.zh: 民出不意，蕩產失業，多自經死，然盜鑄遂止。

translations.literal: The people were caught unprepared; many lost their property and livelihoods and hanged themselves, yet illicit casting ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The people were caught unprepared; many were ruined and hanged themselves, yet illicit casting ceased.

sentences.zh: 自康定用兵，移稅輸邊，民力大困，求令輸本州，而轉錢以供邊糴，民受其惠，而兵食亦足。

translations.literal: Since the Kangding campaigns, tax grain had been shifted to the frontier and the people's strength was greatly strained. Qiu ordered that grain be delivered to the home prefecture while money was transported to supply frontier purchases; the people benefited and military provisions were also sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Kangding campaigns, tax grain had been diverted to the frontier and the people were greatly strained. Qiu ordered that grain be delivered within the home prefecture while money was shipped to purchase frontier supplies; the people benefited and military rations were also sufficient.

sentences.zh: 召為戶部副使。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 隴右蕃酋蘭氈獻古渭州地，秦州范祥納之，請繕城屯兵，又括熟戶田，諸羌靳之，相率叛。

translations.literal: The tribal chieftain Lan Zhan of Longyou offered the territory of ancient Weizhou; Fan Xiang of Qinzhou accepted it, requested repairing the city and garrisoning troops, and also requisitioned fields of assimilated households. The various Qiang resented this and rebelled in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal chieftain Lan Zhan of Longyou offered the territory of ancient Weizhou; Fan Xiang of Qinzhou accepted it, requested repairing the city and garrisoning troops, and also requisitioned fields belonging to assimilated households. The various Qiang tribes resented this and rebelled in succession.

sentences.zh: 夏人欲得渭地久，移文來索。

translations.literal: The Xia had long desired to obtain Weizhou and sent a dispatch demanding it.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Xia had long desired Weizhou and sent a dispatch demanding its return.

sentences.zh: 後帥張昇以祥貪利生事，請棄之。

translations.literal: Later the commander Zhang Sheng, on the grounds that Xiang had stirred up trouble out of greed for profit, requested that it be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Later Commander Zhang Sheng, holding that Xiang had stirred up trouble out of greed for profit, requested that the territory be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 詔求往視，求以為城已訖役，且已得而棄，非所以強國威。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Qiu to go inspect; Qiu held that the fortifications were already completed, and that to obtain something and then abandon it was not the way to strengthen national prestige.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Qiu to go and inspect the situation. Qiu argued that the fortifications were already finished, and that to gain territory only to surrender it would not strengthen the nation's prestige.

sentences.zh: 乃詔諭羌眾，反其田，報夏人以渭非其有，不應索，正其封疆而還，兵遂解。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict instructed the Qiang people, restored their fields, and replied to the Xia that Weizhou was not theirs and their demand should not be granted; borders were rectified and the troops withdrew, and the military standoff was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: The court then issued an edict to the Qiang, restored their fields, and told the Western Xia that Weizhou was not theirs and their demand should be refused. After the borders were set right the army withdrew, and the crisis ended.

sentences.zh: 進天章閣待制，陝西都轉運使，加龍圖閣直學士、知慶州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin academician of the Tianzhang Pavilion, made chief transport commissioner of Shaanxi, granted academician in direct attendance at the Longtu Pavilion, and appointed prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin academician of the Tianzhang Pavilion, appointed chief transport commissioner of Shaanxi, granted the title of academician in direct attendance at the Longtu Pavilion, and made prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 環之定邊砦蕃官蘇恩，以小過疑懼而遁，將佐議致討。

translations.literal: Su En, a tribal officer at Dingbian Stockade in Huanzhou, fled in suspicion and fear over a minor offense; the commanders discussed launching a punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Su En, a tribal officer at Dingbian Stockade in Huanzhou, fled in fear over a minor offense. The commanders debated sending troops to punish him.

sentences.zh: 涇原既出師境上，求謂恩非素攜二者，乘以兵，必起邊患。

translations.literal: Jingyuan circuit had already sent troops to the border; Qiu said that En was not by nature a troublemaker, and that sending troops against him would surely stir up frontier troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan circuit had already mobilized troops on the frontier. Qiu said that En was not by nature a troublemaker, and that sending soldiers against him would surely provoke border conflict.

sentences.zh: 但遣裨將從十數卒扣其帳，開以禍福，恩感泣，還砦如初。

translations.literal: He merely sent a vice general with a dozen or so soldiers to visit his tent and explain the consequences of fortune and misfortune; En wept in gratitude and returned to the stockade as before.
translations.idiomatic: He sent only a vice general with a dozen soldiers to En's tent to explain the consequences of compliance and defiance. En wept in gratitude and returned to the stockade as before.

sentences.zh: 入判太常寺，權發遣開封府，遷樞密直學士、知定州，復以龍圖閣學士權開封。

translations.literal: He entered the capital to serve as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, with concurrent authority over the Kaifeng prefecture; he was transferred to privy council academician and prefect of Dingzhou, and again served as Longtu academician with concurrent control of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with concurrent authority over Kaifeng, was transferred to privy council academician and prefect of Dingzhou, and later served again as Longtu academician with concurrent control of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 求本有吏能幹局，至是，春秋浸高，且病聵。

translations.literal: Qiu had originally possessed the ability and resolve of an administrator, but by this time his years were advancing and he was afflicted with deafness.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu had once been a capable and decisive administrator, but by now he was growing old and suffering from deafness.

sentences.zh: 三司大將錢吉密殺妹，為鄰所告，求不能決，反坐告者；

translations.literal: Qian Ji, a senior officer of the Three Departments, secretly killed his younger sister and was reported by a neighbor; Qiu could not resolve the case and instead punished the accuser;
translations.idiomatic: Qian Ji, a senior officer of the Three Departments, secretly murdered his younger sister and was reported by a neighbor. Qiu could not decide the case and instead punished the accuser;

sentences.zh: 又斷獄數差失。

translations.literal: He also made several errors in deciding cases.
translations.idiomatic: He also made several mistakes in deciding legal cases.

sentences.zh: 御史言其不勝任，出知兗州。

translations.literal: The censorate reported that he was unfit for office, and he was sent out as prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate reported that he was no longer fit for office, and he was sent out as prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 張景憲

translations.literal: Zhang Jingxian
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingxian

sentences.zh: 張景憲，字正國，河南人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jingxian, styled Zhengguo, was a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingxian, whose courtesy name was Zhengguo, came from Henan.

sentences.zh: 以父師德任淮南轉運副使。

translations.literal: Through his father Shide's patronage he became vice transport commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father Shide's influence he was appointed vice transport commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 山陽令鄭昉贓累巨萬，親戚多要人，景憲首案治，流之嶺外，貪吏望風引去。

translations.literal: Zheng Fang, magistrate of Shanyang, had accumulated embezzlements reaching tens of thousands; his relatives included many powerful men. Jingxian took the lead in investigating and had him exiled beyond the Ling ranges; corrupt officials fled at the news.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Fang, magistrate of Shanyang, had embezzled a fortune, and his relatives included many powerful men. Jingxian took the lead in prosecuting him and had him exiled beyond the Ling ranges, whereupon corrupt officials fled at the news.

sentences.zh: 徙京西、東轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to transport commissioner of the Jingxi and Jingdong circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as transport commissioner of the Jingxi and Jingdong circuits.

sentences.zh: 王逵居鄆，專持吏短長，求請賄謝如所欲，景憲上其惡，編置宿州。

translations.literal: Wang Kui resided in Yunzhou and specialized in holding officials' faults over them, demanding bribes and gratuities as he wished; Jingxian reported his crimes and had him assigned to Suzhou in penal exile.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kui lived in Yunzhou and made a trade of holding officials' faults over them, demanding bribes and favors at will. Jingxian reported his crimes and had him assigned to Suzhou in penal exile.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，為戶部副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xining era he became vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xining era he was appointed vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 韓絳築撫寧、囉兀兩城，帝命景憲往視。

translations.literal: Han Jiang built the two forts of Funing and Luowu; the emperor ordered Jingxian to go inspect them.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jiang built the two forts of Funing and Luowu, and the emperor ordered Jingxian to go and inspect them.

sentences.zh: 始受詔，即言城不可守，固不待到而後知也。

translations.literal: As soon as he received the edict he declared that the forts could not be held—he certainly did not need to wait until he arrived to know it.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he received the edict he declared that the forts could not be held. He hardly needed to visit them in person to know that.

sentences.zh: 未幾，撫寧陷。

translations.literal: Before long Funing fell.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Funing fell.

sentences.zh: 至延安，又言：「囉兀邈然孤城，鑿井無水，將何以守？

translations.literal: When he reached Yan'an he again said: "Luowu is a remote isolated fort; wells are dug yet yield no water—how is it to be defended?"
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Yan'an he again said, "Luowu is a distant, isolated fort. Wells are dug but yield no water. How can it be defended?"

sentences.zh: 臣在道，所見師勞民困之狀非一，願罷徒勞之役，廢無用之城，嚴飭邊將為守計。

translations.literal: On the road I have witnessed more than one instance of exhausted troops and distressed commoners; I pray that pointless labor be halted, useless forts abandoned, and frontier generals strictly ordered to plan for defense."
translations.idiomatic: On the road I have seen repeated signs of exhausted troops and distressed commoners. I pray that pointless labor be stopped, useless forts abandoned, and frontier generals strictly ordered to plan for defense."

sentences.zh: 令邊郡召生羌，與之金帛、官爵，恐黠羌多詐，緩急或為內應，宜亟止之。

translations.literal: Border prefectures have been ordered to summon native Qiang and grant them gold, silk, and official ranks; I fear that cunning Qiang will mostly feign loyalty and may serve as internal collaborators in an emergency—this should be stopped at once."
translations.idiomatic: Border prefectures have been ordered to summon native Qiang and grant them gold, silk, and official rank. I fear that many cunning Qiang will feign loyalty and may serve as internal collaborators in an emergency. This should be stopped at once."

sentences.zh: 」陝西轉運司議，欲限半歲令民悉納錢於官，而易以交子。

translations.literal: The Shaanxi transport commission proposed that within half a year the people be required to turn in all cash to the government in exchange for jiaozi notes.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaanxi transport commission proposed that within half a year the people be required to turn in all cash to the government in exchange for jiaozi paper notes.

sentences.zh: 景憲言：「此法可行於蜀耳，若施之陝西，民將無以為命。

translations.literal: Jingxian said: "This method may work in Shu alone; if applied in Shaanxi, the people will have no means to live."
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian said, "This method may work in Shu, but if applied in Shaanxi the people will have no way to live."

sentences.zh: 」其後卒不行。

translations.literal: In the end it was never implemented.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the proposal was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 加集賢殿修撰，為河東都轉運使。

translations.literal: He was granted the title of compiler in the Jixian Hall and appointed chief transport commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the title of compiler in the Jixian Hall and appointed chief transport commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 議者欲分河東為兩路，景憲言：「本道地肥磽相雜，州縣貧富亦異，正宜有無相通，分之不便。

translations.literal: Some proposed dividing Hedong into two circuits; Jingxian said: "This circuit has fertile and barren land mixed together, and its prefectures and counties differ in wealth and poverty—it is precisely suited to mutual aid between haves and have-nots; dividing it would be inconvenient."
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed dividing Hedong into two circuits. Jingxian said, "This circuit mixes fertile and barren land, and its prefectures and counties differ in wealth and poverty. It is precisely suited to mutual aid between rich and poor regions; dividing it would be impractical."

sentences.zh: 」議遂寢，改知瀛州，上言：「比歲多不登，民積逋欠。

translations.literal: The proposal was shelved; he was transferred to prefect of Yingzhou and submitted a memorial: "In recent years harvests have often failed, and the people have accumulated arrears."
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped. He was transferred to prefect of Yingzhou and submitted a memorial saying, "In recent years harvests have often failed, and the people have accumulated tax arrears."

sentences.zh: 今方小稔，而官督使並償，道路流言，其禍乃甚於凶歲。

translations.literal: Now there has just been a modest harvest, yet officials are pressing for full repayment at once; rumors along the roads say the harm will exceed that of a famine year."
translations.idiomatic: There has just been a modest harvest, yet officials are pressing for full repayment at once. Rumors along the roads say the harm will exceed that of a famine year."

sentences.zh: 願以寬假。

translations.literal: I pray for leniency and deferral."
translations.idiomatic: I pray for leniency and deferral."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，仍下其事。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed and issued orders accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and issued orders to that effect.

sentences.zh: 元豐初年，知河陽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanfeng era he became prefect of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanfeng era he was appointed prefect of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 時方討西南蠻，景憲入辭，因言：「小醜跳梁，殆邊吏擾之耳。

translations.literal: When a campaign against the southwestern barbarians was underway, Jingxian entered to take leave and said: "These petty troublemakers are causing disturbances—likely it is merely border officials harassing them."
translations.idiomatic: While a campaign against the southwestern barbarians was underway, Jingxian entered to take leave and said, "These petty troublemakers are causing disturbances—likely it is merely border officials harassing them."

sentences.zh: 且其巢穴險阻，若動兵遠征，萬一饋餉不繼，則我師坐困矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, their lairs are rugged and perilous; if troops are mobilized for a distant expedition and supplies should fail, our army will be trapped in place."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, their lairs are rugged and hard to reach. If troops are sent on a distant expedition and supplies fail, our army will be trapped in place."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿言是也，然朝廷有不得已者。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What you say is correct, yet the court has reasons beyond its control."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What you say is correct, yet the court has reasons beyond its control."

sentences.zh: 」明年，徙同州，以太中大夫卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: The following year he was transferred to Tongzhou and died with the rank of Grand Master of Palace Attendance at the age of seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Tongzhou and died with the rank of Grand Master of Palace Attendance at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 景憲在仁宗朝為部使者，時吏治尚寬，獨多舉刺；

translations.literal: During the Renzong reign Jingxian served as a circuit commissioner; when official discipline was generally lenient, he alone frequently exposed and impeached wrongdoing;
translations.idiomatic: During the Renzong reign Jingxian served as a circuit commissioner. When official discipline was generally lenient, he alone frequently exposed and impeached wrongdoing;

sentences.zh: 及熙寧以來，吏治峻急，景憲反濟以寬。

translations.literal: When from the Xining era onward official discipline became stern and severe, Jingxian instead tempered it with leniency.
translations.idiomatic: When from the Xining era onward official discipline became stern and severe, Jingxian instead tempered it with leniency.

sentences.zh: 方新法之行，不劾一人。

translations.literal: During the implementation of the New Policies he impeached not a single person.
translations.idiomatic: During the implementation of the New Policies he impeached not a single person.

sentences.zh: 居官不畏強禦，非公事不及執政之門。

translations.literal: In office he did not fear the powerful; except on public business he never visited the doors of those in power.
translations.idiomatic: In office he did not fear the powerful, and except on public business he never visited the doors of those in power.

sentences.zh: 自負所守，於人少許可，母卒，一夕鬚髮盡白，世以此稱之。

translations.literal: Confident in his principles, he rarely approved of others; when his mother died, overnight his beard and hair turned completely white, and the world praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his principles, he rarely approved of others. When his mother died, his beard and hair turned completely white overnight, and the world praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 竇卞，字彥法，曹州冤句人，進士第二，通判汝州。

translations.literal: Dou Bian, styled Yanfa, was a man of Yuanju in Caozhou; he placed second in the jinshi examination and became vice-prefect of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Bian, whose courtesy name was Yanfa, came from Yuanju in Caozhou. He placed second in the jinshi examination and was appointed vice-prefect of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 秦悼王葬汝，宗室來祔者眾，役兵三千，郡守林濰以汝與其鄉近，因使輦薪芻、鐵石致其家。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhaohui of Qin was buried at Ruzhou, many imperial clansmen came to join their tombs; three thousand conscript soldiers were employed. Prefect Lin Wei, because Ruzhou was near his home district, had them haul firewood, fodder, iron, and stone to his house.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhaohui of Qin was buried at Ruzhou, many imperial clansmen came to join their tombs, and three thousand conscript soldiers were employed. Prefect Lin Wei, because Ruzhou was near his home district, had them haul firewood, fodder, iron, and stone to his house.

sentences.zh: 眾怨憤，謀殺濰，會日暮門閉，不果，遂挾大校叛。

translations.literal: The troops resented this; they plotted to kill Wei, but at dusk the gates closed and the plan failed, so they seized a senior officer and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The troops resented this and plotted to kill Wei, but at dusk the gates closed and the plan failed, so they seized a senior officer and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 卞啟關招諭之，曰：「汝曹特醉酒狂呼爾，毋恐。

translations.literal: Bian opened the gates and summoned them to reason, saying: "You have merely been shouting drunkenly—do not be afraid."
translations.idiomatic: Bian opened the gates and summoned them to reason, saying, "You have merely been shouting drunkenly. Do not be afraid."

sentences.zh: 」眾少定，乃密推首惡羈之，請於朝，詔濰致仕，悉配徙亂者。

translations.literal: When the crowd had calmed somewhat, he secretly identified the ringleaders and detained them; he reported to the court, an edict ordered Wei to retire, and all the mutineers were assigned to penal exile.
translations.idiomatic: When the crowd had calmed somewhat, he secretly identified the ringleaders and detained them. He reported to the court, an edict ordered Wei to retire, and all the mutineers were sent into penal exile.

sentences.zh: 加集賢校理、知太常院，知絳州，開封府推官。

translations.literal: He was granted the title of collator in the Jixian Hall, made director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, appointed prefect of Jiangzhou, and served as investigating officer of the Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the title of collator in the Jixian Hall, made director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, appointed prefect of Jiangzhou, and served as investigating officer of the Kaifeng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 方禁銷金為衣，皇城卒捕得之，屬卞治，以中禁為言。

translations.literal: When the prohibition on melting gold for clothing was in force, an imperial-city soldier was caught doing so and the case was assigned to Bian; the soldier cited the imperial precinct as grounds for leniency.
translations.idiomatic: While the prohibition on melting gold for clothing was in force, an imperial-city soldier was caught doing so and the case was assigned to Bian. The soldier cited the imperial precinct as grounds for leniency.

sentences.zh: 奏曰：「真宗行此制，自掖廷始，今不正以法，無以示天下，且非祖宗立法意。

translations.literal: Bian memorialized: "Emperor Zhenzong instituted this rule beginning with the inner palace; if it is not corrected by law now, there will be no way to show the realm, and it would not accord with the intent of the founders in establishing the law."
translations.idiomatic: Bian memorialized, "Emperor Zhenzong instituted this rule beginning with the inner palace. If it is not corrected by law now, there will be no way to show the realm, and it would not accord with the founders' intent in establishing the law."

sentences.zh: 」英宗曰：「然。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong said: "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong said, "So it is."

sentences.zh: 文王『刑於寡妻，至於兄弟，以御於家邦』，正謂是也。

translations.literal: King Wen said, 'Begin with your wife, extend to your brothers, and thereby govern family and state'—that is precisely what is meant."
translations.idiomatic: King Wen said, 'Begin with your wife, extend to your brothers, and thereby govern family and state'—that is precisely what is meant."

sentences.zh: 」從其請。

translations.literal: His request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 出知深州。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，河決滹沱，水及郡城，地大震，流民自恩、冀來，踵相接，卞發常平粟食之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xining the Hutuo River burst its banks; water reached the prefectural city and a great earthquake occurred; refugees from En and Ji came one after another, and Bian issued grain from the Ever-Normal Granary to feed them.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xining era the Hutuo River burst its banks. Water reached the prefectural city and a great earthquake struck. Refugees from En and Ji arrived in an unbroken stream, and Bian issued grain from the Ever-Normal Granary to feed them.

sentences.zh: 吏白擅發且獲罪，卞曰：「俟請而得報，民死矣。

translations.literal: Clerks reported that distributing it without authorization would incur punishment; Bian said: "If we wait to request permission and receive a reply, the people will be dead."
translations.idiomatic: Clerks warned that distributing grain without authorization would incur punishment. Bian said, "If we wait to request permission and receive a reply, the people will be dead."

sentences.zh: 吾寧以一身活數萬人。

translations.literal: I would rather save tens of thousands of lives with my own person."
translations.idiomatic: I would rather save tens of thousands of lives at the cost of my own."

sentences.zh: 」尋以請，詔許之。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he submitted the request, and an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he submitted the request, and an edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 外間訛言水大至，卞下令敢言者斬。

translations.literal: Outside rumors spread that great floods were coming; Bian ordered that anyone who spread such talk would be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread outside that great floods were coming. Bian ordered that anyone who spread such talk would be executed.

sentences.zh: 一日，復報大水且至，吏請閉門，卞不可，既而果妄。

translations.literal: One day reports again came that great floods were imminent; officials asked to close the gates, but Bian refused; in the end the reports proved false.
translations.idiomatic: One day reports again came that great floods were imminent. Officials asked to close the gates, but Bian refused. In the end the reports proved false.

sentences.zh: 時發六州卒築武彊，陳卒惰，主者笞之，不服。

translations.literal: At the time troops from six prefectures were conscripted to build embankments at Wuqiang; soldiers from Chen were lazy; the overseer beat them and they refused to submit.
translations.idiomatic: At the time troops from six prefectures were conscripted to build embankments at Wuqiang. Soldiers from Chen were lazy; the overseer beat them, and they refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 卞曰：「廂兵犯將校，法不至重，然興役聚工，不可拘以常法。

translations.literal: Bian said: "For garrison soldiers to offend their officers, the law does not prescribe severe punishment, yet when labor is mobilized and workers gathered, ordinary law cannot be rigidly applied."
translations.idiomatic: Bian said, "For garrison soldiers to offend their officers, the law does not prescribe severe punishment, yet when labor is mobilized and workers gathered, ordinary law cannot be rigidly applied."

sentences.zh: 」命斬之以聞，有詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: He ordered them beheaded and reported it; an edict commended him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them beheaded and reported it to the court. An edict commended him.

sentences.zh: 還為戶部判官、同修起居注，進天章閣待制，判昭文館、將作監。

translations.literal: He returned to serve as judicial official of the Ministry of Revenue, concurrent compiler of the Daily Records, was promoted to Hanlin academician of the Tianzhang Pavilion, and served as vice director of the Zhaowen Hall and the Directorate of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to serve as judicial official of the Ministry of Revenue and concurrent compiler of the Daily Records, was promoted to Hanlin academician of the Tianzhang Pavilion, and served as vice director of the Zhaowen Hall and the Directorate of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 始，卞官汝時，與殿直王永年者相接頗厚，及在京師，永年求監金曜門庫，卞為禱提舉揚繪，繪薦為之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Bian served at Ruzhou, he had been quite close with palace attendant Wang Yongnian; when in the capital Yongnian sought to supervise the Jinyao Gate treasury, and Bian pleaded with intendant Yang Hui, who recommended him for the post.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Bian served at Ruzhou, he had been quite close with palace attendant Wang Yongnian. When in the capital Yongnian sought to supervise the Jinyao Gate treasury, and Bian pleaded with intendant Yang Hui, who recommended him for the post.

sentences.zh: 永年置酒於家，延繪、卞至，出其妻侑飲，且時致薄餉。

translations.literal: Yongnian set out wine at his home, invited Hui and Bian, had his wife assist in serving drinks, and from time to time sent them small gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Yongnian set out wine at his home, invited Hui and Bian, had his wife assist in serving drinks, and from time to time sent them small gifts.

sentences.zh: 永年以事繫獄死，御史發其私，卞坐奪職，提舉靈仙觀。

translations.literal: Yongnian died in prison over a matter; the censorate exposed his private dealings, and Bian was stripped of office and appointed superintendent of the Lingxian Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Yongnian died in prison over a matter. The censorate exposed his private dealings, and Bian was stripped of office and appointed superintendent of the Lingxian Abbey.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十五。

translations.literal: He died at the age of forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-five.

sentences.zh: 張瓌，字唐公，洎之孫也。

translations.literal: Zhang Gui, styled Tangong, was the grandson of Zhang Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui, whose courtesy name was Tangong, was the grandson of Zhang Ji.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，以婦父王欽若嫌，召試學士院，賜第，除秘閣校理、同知太常禮院。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination; because of his father-in-law Wang Qinruo's influence he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy for examination, granted a ranked degree, and appointed collator in the Secretariat Pavilion and vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, but because of his father-in-law Wang Qinruo's influence he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy for examination, granted a ranked degree, and appointed collator in the Secretariat Pavilion and vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 諡錢惟演曰「文墨」，其子撾登聞鼓上訴，仁宗使問狀，瓌條奏甚切，朝廷不能奪，乃賜諡曰「思」。

translations.literal: The posthumous title "Wenmo" was conferred on Qian Weiyan; his son beat the Drum of Direct Appeal and petitioned; Renzong sent someone to inquire into the matter; Gui submitted a detailed and forceful memorial; the court could not overturn it and granted the posthumous title "Si" instead.
translations.idiomatic: The posthumous title "Wenmo" was conferred on Qian Weiyan. His son beat the Drum of Direct Appeal and petitioned the throne. Renzong sent someone to inquire into the matter, and Gui submitted a detailed and forceful memorial. The court could not overturn it and granted the posthumous title "Si" instead.

sentences.zh: 溫成廟祠享如神御，請殺其禮。

translations.literal: Sacrifices at the Wencheng Temple were performed as for an imperial ancestral spirit; he requested that the rites be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices at the Wencheng Temple were performed as for an imperial ancestral spirit, and he requested that the rites be reduced.

sentences.zh: 判吏部南曹，為開封府推官、知洪州。

translations.literal: He served as director of the Southern Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel, investigating officer of Kaifeng, and prefect of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director of the Southern Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel, investigating officer of Kaifeng, and prefect of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 營校督役苛急，其徒三百人將以夜殺之。

translations.literal: A construction officer pressed the labor extremely harshly; three hundred of his men planned to kill him by night.
translations.idiomatic: A construction officer drove the laborers with extreme harshness, and three hundred of his men planned to kill him by night.

sentences.zh: 求不獲，持臿譟於門，請易校。

translations.literal: Unable to find him, they brandished spades and raised an uproar at the gate, demanding a replacement officer.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to find him, they brandished spades and raised an uproar at the gate, demanding a replacement officer.

sentences.zh: 瓌召問諭遣，明日，推治黠十人，不為易校。

translations.literal: Gui summoned them, questioned and dismissed them; the next day he prosecuted ten ringleaders but did not replace the officer.
translations.idiomatic: Gui summoned them, questioned them, and sent them away. The next day he prosecuted ten ringleaders but did not replace the officer.

sentences.zh: 積閥當遷，十年不會課，文彥博為言，特遷之。

translations.literal: His accumulated merit qualified him for promotion, but for ten years he received no performance review; Wen Yanbo spoke on his behalf and he was specially promoted.
translations.idiomatic: His accumulated merit qualified him for promotion, but for ten years he received no performance review. Wen Yanbo spoke on his behalf, and he was specially promoted.

sentences.zh: 徙兩浙轉運使，加直史館、知潁州、揚州，即拜淮南轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to transport commissioner of the Liangzhe circuits, granted compiler in the Historiography Institute, appointed prefect of Yingzhou and Yangzhou, and immediately invested as transport commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to transport commissioner of the Liangzhe circuits, granted compiler in the Historiography Institute, appointed prefect of Yingzhou and Yangzhou, and immediately invested as transport commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 三司下諸道責羨財，淮南獨上金九錢，三司使怒，移文譙切，瓌以賦數民貧對。

translations.literal: The Three Departments ordered all circuits to submit surplus funds; Huainan alone submitted nine cents of gold; the Three Departments commissioner was enraged and sent a sharply worded dispatch; Gui replied that tax quotas were high and the people were poor.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments ordered all circuits to submit surplus funds. Huainan alone submitted nine cents of gold. The Three Departments commissioner was enraged and sent a sharply worded dispatch, to which Gui replied that tax quotas were high and the people were poor.

sentences.zh: 入修起居注、知制誥。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as compiler of the Daily Records and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as compiler of the Daily Records and drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 草故相劉沆贈官制，頗言其附會取顯位。

translations.literal: He drafted the edict conferring posthumous office on the late chief councillor Liu Hang, stating rather plainly that Hang had curried favor to obtain high rank.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted the edict conferring posthumous office on the late chief councillor Liu Hang, stating rather plainly that Hang had curried favor to obtain high rank.

sentences.zh: 沆子瑾帥子弟婦女衰絰詣闕，哭訴瓌挾私怨，且醜詆其人。

translations.literal: Hang's son Jin led sons, daughters, and daughters-in-law in mourning garments to the palace gate, weeping and accusing Gui of personal spite and slandering his father's character.
translations.idiomatic: Hang's son Jin led sons, daughters, and daughters-in-law in mourning garments to the palace gate, weeping and accusing Gui of personal spite and slandering his father's character.

sentences.zh: 執政以褒贈乃恩典，瓌不當為貶詞，出知黃州，然瑾亦竟不敢請父諡。

translations.literal: The chief councillors held that conferring honors was a grace and Gui should not have used deprecatory language; he was sent out as prefect of Huangzhou, yet Jin also in the end dared not request a posthumous title for his father.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councillors held that conferring honors was an act of grace and that Gui should not have used deprecatory language. He was sent out as prefect of Huangzhou, yet Jin also in the end dared not request a posthumous title for his father.

sentences.zh: 還判流內銓。

translations.literal: He returned to serve as director of the Outer Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to serve as director of the Outer Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 英宗時，論第在先朝乞蚤定儲副者，進左諫議大夫、翰林侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Yingzong, in ranking those who in the previous reign had petitioned early for designation of the heir apparent, he was promoted to Left Remonstrance Councillor and Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yingzong, in ranking those who in the previous reign had petitioned early for designation of the heir apparent, he was promoted to Left Remonstrance Councillor and Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾又訟其判銓日，調其子不應法，復出濠州。

translations.literal: Liu Jin again sued him, alleging that when he directed the bureau he had assigned his own son in violation of the regulations, and he was again sent out as prefect of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin again sued him, alleging that when he directed the bureau he had assigned his own son in violation of the regulations, and he was again sent out as prefect of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 歷應天府、河南、河陽，請為太平州。

translations.literal: He served successively at Yingtian Prefecture, Henan, and Heyang, and requested appointment to Taiping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively at Yingtian Prefecture, Henan, and Heyang, and requested appointment to Taiping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 瓌平生薦士，後雖不如所舉，未嚐以令自首，故再坐削階。

translations.literal: Throughout his life Gui recommended scholars; even when they later did not live up to his recommendation, he never ordered them to confess, and for this he twice suffered demotion in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his life Gui recommended scholars. Even when they later did not live up to his recommendation, he never ordered them to confess, and for this he twice suffered demotion in rank.

sentences.zh: 當官遇事輒言，觸忤勢要，至屢黜，終不悔。

translations.literal: In office he spoke out whenever matters arose, offending the powerful; though repeatedly dismissed he never regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: In office he spoke out whenever matters arose, offending the powerful. Though repeatedly dismissed, he never regretted it.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 孫瑜，字叔禮，博平人。

translations.literal: Sun Yu, styled Shuli, was a man of Boping.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yu, whose courtesy name was Shuli, came from Boping.

sentences.zh: 以父任為將作監主簿，賈昌朝薦為崇文檢討、同知禮院、開封府判官。

translations.literal: Through his father's patronage he became chief clerk of the Directorate of Public Works; Jia Changchao recommended him as collator in the Chongwen Hall, vice director of the Court of Rites, and vice magistrate of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's patronage he became chief clerk of the Directorate of Public Works. Jia Changchao recommended him as collator in the Chongwen Hall, vice director of the Court of Rites, and vice magistrate of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 使契丹，適西討捷書至，館伴要入賀，啖以厚餉，瑜辭以奉使有指，不肯賀。

translations.literal: On a mission to the Khitan, news of a western campaign victory arrived; the host commissioner wished to enter the capital to offer congratulations and tempted him with lavish gifts; Yu declined on the grounds that his mission had specific instructions and refused to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to the Khitan, news of a western campaign victory arrived. The host commissioner wished to enter the capital to offer congratulations and tempted him with lavish gifts, but Yu declined on the grounds that his mission had specific instructions and refused to congratulate.

sentences.zh: 加秘閣校理、兩浙轉運使。

translations.literal: He was granted collator in the Secretariat Pavilion and appointed transport commissioner of the Liangzhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted collator in the Secretariat Pavilion and appointed transport commissioner of the Liangzhe circuits.

sentences.zh: 入辭，仁宗訪其家世，謂曰：「卿孫奭子邪？

translations.literal: Entering to take leave, Renzong inquired into his family background and said: "Are you the son of Sun Shi?"
translations.idiomatic: Entering to take leave, Renzong inquired into his family background and said, "Are you the son of Sun Shi?"

sentences.zh: 奭，大儒也，久以道輔朕。

translations.literal: Shi was a great Confucian who long assisted me with the Way."
translations.idiomatic: Shi was a great Confucian who long assisted me with the Way."

sentences.zh: 」因面賜金紫。

translations.literal: He was thereupon granted gold seal and purple robe in person.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon granted a gold seal and purple robe in person.

sentences.zh: 先是，郡縣倉庾以斗斛大小為奸，瑜奏均其制，黜吏之亡狀者，民大喜。

translations.literal: Previously, prefectural and county granaries had cheated with differing sizes of pecks and hus; Yu memorialized to standardize the measures, dismissed dishonest clerks, and the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, prefectural and county granaries had cheated by using pecks and hus of differing sizes. Yu memorialized to standardize the measures, dismissed dishonest clerks, and the people were greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 有言其變新器非便，下遷知曹州。

translations.literal: Someone reported that changing to the new vessels was inconvenient; he was demoted and made prefect of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When someone reported that his switch to the new measuring vessels was impractical, he was demoted and appointed prefect of Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 尋有言瑜所作量法均一誠便者，乃還其元資，徙知蔡州，毀吳元濟像，以其祠事裴度。

translations.literal: Soon someone reported that Yu's standardized measures were truly convenient; his original rank was restored, he was transferred to be prefect of Caizhou, destroyed Wu Yuanji's image, and converted the shrine to honor Pei Du.
translations.idiomatic: Before long someone reported that Yu's uniform system of measures was genuinely convenient; his original rank was restored, he was transferred to Caizhou, the image of Wu Yuanji was destroyed, and the shrine was rededicated to Pei Du.

sentences.zh: 大水緣城隙入，瑜使囊沙數千扞其衝，城得弗壞。

translations.literal: Great flood water entered through gaps in the city wall; Yu had thousands of sandbags used to block the impact, and the wall was not destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When floodwaters poured in through gaps in the city wall, Yu had thousands of sandbags piled to break the force of the current, and the wall held.

sentences.zh: 更相、兗、濰、單四州，累官工部侍郎，卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: He served successively in the four prefectures of Xiang, Yan, Wei, and Shan, rose cumulatively to Vice Minister of Works, and died at age seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of Xiang, Yan, Wei, and Shan, rose through the ranks to Vice Minister of Works, and died at seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 始，奭之亡，朝廷錄其子孫，時瑜之子為諸孫長，瑜曰：「吾忍因父喪而官吾子乎？

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Shi died, the court enrolled his descendants for office; at the time Yu's son was the eldest among the grandsons. Yu said, "How could I bear to obtain office for my son on account of my father's death?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shi died, the court enrolled his descendants for office; Yu's son was then the eldest of the grandsons. Yu said, "How could I bear to secure an appointment for my son because of my father's death?

sentences.zh: 」以兄之孤上之。

translations.literal: " He presented his elder brother's orphaned son instead.
translations.idiomatic: " Instead he submitted his elder brother's orphaned son.

sentences.zh: 瑜天資整敏，齊家以嚴稱。

translations.literal: Yu was naturally orderly and quick-witted, and was known for strictness in managing his household.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was by nature disciplined and sharp, and was renowned for the strictness with which he ran his household.

sentences.zh: 善與人交，一受知終身不易。

translations.literal: He was skilled at friendship; once he received someone's trust, he never changed for life.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in friendship: once he had formed a bond of trust, he never broke it for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 所薦士有過，或教使自言，曰：「已知之而復擠之，吾不為也。」

translations.literal: When men he had recommended had faults, some urged him to report them himself; he said, "Having already known them and then to press them down — I will not do that."
translations.idiomatic: When a man he had recommended fell into error, some urged him to denounce the man himself. He said, "Having once trusted him, I will not turn and crush him — I will not do that."

sentences.zh: 論曰：宋至神宗，承平百餘年，風行政成，士皆守官稱職，雖上之化，亦下之氣習使然也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: From the Song to Emperor Shenzong, after more than a hundred years of peace, customs flourished and government succeeded; scholars all kept to their posts and fulfilled their duties — though this was due to the transformation from above, it was also because the temper of those below made it so.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary runs thus: By the time of Emperor Shenzong, the Song had enjoyed more than a century of peace; customs flourished and government prospered, and officials kept their posts and did their work. This owed something to imperial example, but also to the habits that had taken root below.

sentences.zh: 當時仕於朝廷，出守方嶽，持節一道，專對四方者，各有其人，其政跡且多可紀，自顓至瑜是已。

translations.literal: At that time those who served at court, went out to guard the great commanderies, held credentials over a circuit, or handled foreign affairs alone — each had his man, and their political records were mostly worth recording, from Zhuan to Yu — such were they.
translations.idiomatic: In that age, whether one served at court, governed a great prefecture, held authority over a circuit, or handled foreign affairs on one's own, there was a man for each task, and most of their records of office are worth recounting — from Zhuan to Yu, these were such men.

sentences.zh: 顓能折夏人，屈元昊使者；

translations.literal: Zhuan could subdue the Xia people and humiliate Yuanhao's envoys;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuan could break the pride of the Xia and put Yuanhao's envoys to shame;

sentences.zh: 參擊貪除害，乃心邊事；

translations.literal: Can struck at greed and removed harm, his heart set on frontier affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Can struck down the greedy and cleared away harm, his heart fixed on frontier affairs;

sentences.zh: 申錫除凶黨，詆權幸；

translations.literal: Shenxi eliminated evil factions and denounced the powerful favorites;
translations.idiomatic: Shenxi uprooted vicious factions and denounced the powerful favorites at court;

sentences.zh: 求黥黠吏，禁盜鑄；
