translations.literal: Shu Dan had been led home by an official torch; the chief ministers wanted to convict him of misappropriating public property.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Dan had been escorted home by an official torch, and the chief ministers wished to convict him of misappropriating public property.

sentences.zh: 吉甫謂不可，執政怒，移獄他所，吉甫亦就辨。

translations.literal: Jifu said this would not stand; the chief ministers were angered and moved the case elsewhere, but Jifu went as well to argue the point.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu said this would not stand. The chief ministers were angered and moved the case elsewhere, but Jifu followed to argue the point himself.

sentences.zh: 亶乃用飲食論罪，不以燭也。

translations.literal: Shu was convicted on food-and-drink charges instead, not on the torch.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was convicted on charges of food and drink instead, not on the torch.

sentences.zh: 南郊起幔城，役卒急於畢事，董役者責之曰：「此殆類白露屋耳。

translations.literal: When the tent city was raised for the Southern Suburban Sacrifice, conscript laborers were pressed to finish quickly; the overseer scolded them, saying, "This is almost like a Bailu house."
translations.idiomatic: When the tent city was raised for the Southern Suburban Sacrifice, the conscript laborers were pressed to finish quickly. The overseer scolded them, saying, "This is almost like a Bailu house."

sentences.zh: 」卒訴之。

translations.literal: The laborers lodged a complaint.
translations.idiomatic: The laborers lodged a complaint.

sentences.zh: 吏當非所宜言論死。

translations.literal: The clerks ruled that the speech was inappropriate and merited death.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks ruled that such speech was impermissible and merited death.

sentences.zh: 吉甫謂非咒詛不應死，遂求對。

translations.literal: Jifu held that absent cursing or imprecation, death was not warranted, and requested an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu held that without cursing or imprecation death was not warranted, and requested an audience with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 神宗怒曰：「得非為白露屋事來邪？

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong said angrily, "Have you come for the Bailu house affair?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong said angrily, "Have you come about the Bailu house affair?"

sentences.zh: 」吉甫從容敷陳，不少懾，帝為霽怒，其人得釋。

translations.literal: Jifu calmly laid out his argument without the least timidity; the emperor's anger cleared, and the man was released.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu calmly laid out his argument without the least timidity. The emperor's anger cleared, and the man was released.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾南遷，所過，郡守有延館之者，走馬使上聞，詔鞫之。

translations.literal: When Su Shi was exiled to the south, at one stop a prefect had lodged him; a mounted courier reported this to the throne, and an edict ordered an investigation.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi was exiled to the south, a prefect at one stop had lodged him. A mounted courier reported this to the throne, and an edict ordered an investigation.

sentences.zh: 吉甫議當笞，宰相章惇不悅。

translations.literal: Jifu argued that flogging was the proper penalty; Chief Councillor Zhang Dun was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu argued that flogging was the proper penalty, but Chief Councillor Zhang Dun was displeased.

sentences.zh: 吉甫曰：「法如是，難以增加成罪。

translations.literal: Jifu said, "The law is as it is — guilt cannot be piled on beyond it."
translations.idiomatic: Jifu said, "The law is as it is; guilt cannot be piled on beyond it."

sentences.zh: 」卒從笞。

translations.literal: In the end flogging was imposed.
translations.idiomatic: In the end flogging was imposed.

sentences.zh: 太倉火，議誅守者十餘人，亦爭之，皆得不死。

translations.literal: When the Imperial Granary burned, more than ten keepers were proposed for execution; he contested this too, and all were spared death.
translations.idiomatic: When the Imperial Granary burned, more than ten keepers were proposed for execution. Jifu contested this as well, and all were spared death.

sentences.zh: 其持論寬平，大抵類此。

translations.literal: His positions were lenient and evenhanded; most cases were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His positions were lenient and evenhanded; most of his cases were of this kind.

sentences.zh: 請知齊州、梓州。

translations.literal: He requested appointment as governor of Qizhou and Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He requested appointment as governor of Qizhou and Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 梓在東川為壯藩，戶口最盛。

translations.literal: Zizhou was the strongest fortress of Eastern Chuan and had the largest population.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhou was the strongest prefecture of Eastern Chuan and had the largest population.

sentences.zh: 轉運使欲增折配以取羨餘。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner wished to increase the supplementary tax levy to extract surplus revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner wished to increase the supplementary tax levy to extract surplus revenue.

sentences.zh: 吉甫謂其僚曰：「民力竭矣，一增之後，不可復減，吾寧貽使者怒，忍為國斂怨、為民基禍哉。

translations.literal: Jifu told his colleagues, "The people's strength is exhausted; once a levy is raised it cannot be lowered again. I would rather provoke the envoy's anger than bear the state's accumulated resentment or lay ruin for the people."
translations.idiomatic: Jifu told his colleagues, "The people's strength is exhausted. Once a levy is raised it cannot be lowered again. I would rather provoke the envoy's anger than heap resentment on the state or lay ruin upon the people."

sentences.zh: 」竟卻之。

translations.literal: In the end he refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he refused.

sentences.zh: 歷提點梓州路京畿刑獄、開封少尹、知同、邢、漢三州，以中大夫卒，年七十。

translations.literal: He served successively as Judicial Commissioner for the Capital Region of Zizhou Circuit, Junior Administrator of Kaifeng, and governor of the three prefectures of Tong, Xing, and Han; he died with the title of Grand Master of the Palace, at age seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Judicial Commissioner for the Capital Region of Zizhou Circuit, Junior Administrator of Kaifeng, and governor of the three prefectures of Tong, Xing, and Han. He died with the title of Grand Master of the Palace, at age seventy.

sentences.zh: 吉甫老於為吏，廉介不回，但一於用法，士恨其少緣飾云。

translations.literal: Jifu was long experienced in administration, upright and unyielding, but single-minded in applying the law; scholars regretted that he showed so little supple discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu was long experienced in administration, upright and unyielding, yet single-minded in applying the law. Scholars regretted that he showed so little diplomatic polish.

sentences.zh: 論曰：宋取士兼習律令，故儒者以經術潤飾吏事，舉能其官。

translations.literal: The commentators say: The Song recruited scholars trained in both classics and statutes, so Confucians polished administrative affairs with classical learning and generally fulfilled their offices well.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Because the Song recruited scholars trained in both the classics and the statutes, Confucians polished administrative work with classical learning and generally fulfilled their offices well.

sentences.zh: 遵惠政及民，而緩登州婦獄，君子謂之失刑。

translations.literal: Zun's benevolent policies reached the people, yet he was lenient in the Dengzhou wife case — gentlemen called this a failure of penal judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Zun's benevolent policies reached the people, yet he was lenient in the Dengzhou wife case, and gentlemen called this a failure of penal judgment.

sentences.zh: 士宗、象先皆執經勸講，其為刑官，論法平恕，宜哉！

translations.literal: Shizong and Xiangxian both held to the classics and urged moral instruction; as judicial officials their legal reasoning was fair and forgiving — as it should be!
translations.idiomatic: Shizong and Xiangxian both held to the classics and urged moral instruction. As judicial officials their legal reasoning was fair and forgiving — as it should be!

sentences.zh: 璹吏事絕人，民懷其德。

translations.literal: Shu's administrative talent was unmatched; the people cherished his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's administrative talent was unmatched, and the people cherished his virtue.

sentences.zh: 純以微官能著清節，紘議獄必傅經誼，風義藹然。

translations.literal: Chun, though in a minor post, was known for unsullied integrity; Chang, when hearing cases, always grounded his reasoning in classic principles — their moral bearing was luminous.
translations.idiomatic: Chun, though holding a minor post, was known for unsullied integrity; Chang, when hearing cases, always grounded his reasoning in classic principles — their moral bearing was luminous.

sentences.zh: 常坐護危埽，麟定徭、獠，宗望弭萬州之變，皆靖至難之事於談笑間。

translations.literal: Chang sat guarding a perilous embankment; Lin pacified Yao bandits and Liao tribes; Zongwang quelled the Wanzhou mutiny — all settled affairs of the utmost difficulty as if in casual conversation.
translations.idiomatic: Chang sat guarding a perilous embankment; Lin pacified Yao bandits and Liao tribes; Zongwang quelled the Wanzhou mutiny — each settled affairs of the utmost difficulty as if in casual conversation.

sentences.zh: 吉甫一於用法，而廉介不回，有足稱云。

translations.literal: Jifu was single-minded in applying the law, yet upright and unyielding — worth praise, indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu was single-minded in applying the law, yet upright and unyielding — worth praise, indeed.
